why: Every caller idiom the ecosystem actually uses, against a real route table. The last two lines are the trap: params.get() and Map.get() take path-shaped arguments and are not HTTP calls at all - reading .get() without checking the receiver reports both as requests. A path-shaped literal is recorded as an uncertain SIGHTING by design, so what must never appear is a js_call claiming it was requested, or a connected fetch_target.
